scope: Python authoring of both engines. HGL admission rejects any negative relative duration after successful time then payload evaluation and before implicit addition. Zero remains allowed, subject to duplicate-publication rules; past absolute targets are skipped. Explicit arithmetic failure inside a time expression prevents payload evaluation.
limits: The large negative case crosses Python datetime's year-1 bound, not signed 64-bit microsecond arithmetic. Downstream captures are observations at a compute node, not proof of unobserved generator-output mutation or rollback. HGL errors are compared by effects, not by equating a reference duplicate diagnostic with negative-duration admission.
